definition_quote.value: Subject to §§ 11–404 and 11–404.2 of this title, to use any means known in the science of optics or eye care, except surgery: To detect, diagnose, manage, and treat, subject to §§ 11–404 and 11–404.2 of this title, any optical or diseased condition in the human eye and the adnexa of the eye; or To prescribe eyeglasses, lenses, or contact lenses to correct any optical or visual condition in the human eye
definition_quote.quote:
Subject to §§ 11–404 and 11–404.2 of this title, to use any means known in the science of optics or eye care, except surgery:
1.    To detect, diagnose, manage, and treat, subject to §§ 11–404 and 11–404.2 of this title, any optical or diseased condition in the human eye and the adnexa of the eye; or
2.    To prescribe eyeglasses, lenses, or contact lenses to correct any optical or visual condition in the human eye

value: detection, diagnosis, management, and treatment of optical or diseased conditions
prescription of eyeglasses, lenses, or contact lenses
administration of pharmaceutical agents
removal of superficial foreign bodies from the cornea and conjunctiva
diagnosis, treatment, and management of open-angle glaucoma
ordering of cultures and bloodwork testing
ordering and performing of in-office, noninvasive, nonradiographic imaging
methods_authorized.quote: practice optometry includes: The administration of pharmaceutical agents; The removal of superficial foreign bodies from the cornea and conjunctiva; The diagnosis, treatment, and management of open–angle glaucoma; The ordering of cultures and bloodwork testing; and The ordering and performing of in–office, noninvasive, nonradiographic imaging

drug_authority.value: Topical ocular diagnostic pharmaceutical agents (with certification); therapeutic pharmaceutical agents (with therapeutic certification); oral pharmaceutical agents subject to restrictions

surgery_definition.quote: a procedure using any instruments, including lasers, scalpels, needles, cautery, a cryoprobe, or sutures in which human tissue is cut, burned, vaporized, removed, or otherwise permanently altered by any mechanical means, laser, ionizing radiation, ultrasound, or other means

minor_surgical_procedures_authorized.quote: Surgery does not include: Preoperative and postoperative care provided in accordance with §§ 11–404 and 11–404.2 of this title; Nonsurgical light therapies used only for the treatment of meibomian gland disease and vision therapy but not for corneal collagen cross linking; Orthokeratology; A noninvasive procedure to remove a superficial foreign body in accordance with § 11–404.2(d) of this title; Corneal scraping or conjunctival swabs for cultures in accordance with § 11–404.2(e) of this title; Epilating with forceps an eyelash from the eyelid, adnexa, or lacrimal system of a patient; or Noninvasive meibomian gland expression

glaucoma_treatment_authorized.quote: The diagnosis, treatment, and management of open–angle glaucoma

pharmaceutical_certification_required.quote: Unless certified under this section, a licensed optometrist may not administer or prescribe any therapeutic pharmaceutical agents

tiered_license_types.quote: "Diagnostically certified optometrist" means a licensed optometrist who is certified by the Board to administer topical ocular diagnostic pharmaceutical agents to the extent permitted under § 11–404 of this title... "Licensed optometrist" means, unless the context requires otherwise, an optometrist who is licensed by the Board to practice optometry... "Therapeutically certified optometrist" means a licensed optometrist who is certified by the Board to practice optometry to the extent permitted under § 11–404.2 of this title.

value: Diagnostic certification (topical ocular diagnostic pharmaceutical agents)
Therapeutic certification (therapeutic pharmaceutical agents and expanded scope)
specialty_certification_types.quote: "Diagnostically certified optometrist" means a licensed optometrist who is certified by the Board to administer topical ocular diagnostic pharmaceutical agents to the extent permitted under § 11–404 of this title... "Therapeutically certified optometrist" means a licensed optometrist who is certified by the Board to practice optometry to the extent permitted under § 11–404.2 of this title.

pharmacology_training_hours_required.quote: Has successfully completed at least 110 hours of a therapeutic pharmaceutical agents course approved by the Board

referral_to_physician_required.quote: If, while providing optometric services to a patient, an optometrist or diagnostically certified optometrist detects or diagnoses an active eye pathology which the optometrist is not licensed or certified to treat under § 11-404 or § 11-404.2 of this subtitle, the optometrist shall refer the patient to: An ophthalmologist or a therapeutically certified optometrist, as appropriate; The patient's physician; A physician if required under a managed care contract; or A hospital emergency room or ambulatory surgical center if necessary

comanagement_with_ophthalmologist_requir.quote: A therapeutically certified optometrist who treats a patient with open–angle glaucoma in accordance with this section shall refer the patient to an ophthalmologist for an examination within 3 months after the initial diagnosis or presentation to the therapeutically certified optometrist unless the intraocular pressure has been reduced 20% or more from the initial pressure

contact_lens_prescription_expiration_yea.quote: an expiration date for the replacement contact lens prescription of not more than 24 months from the time the patient was first examined

spectacle_prescription_release_required.quote: Upon the request of a patient of a licensed optometrist, and without cost to the patient, the licensed optometrist shall provide the patient's replacement contact lens prescription to the patient or the patient's designee

patient_record_retention_years.quote: A person other than a licensed optometrist who fills a contact lens prescription shall maintain a record of that prescription for 5 years
